title: Thanksgiving Dinner Words
cardDescription: Gather familiar words for an American Thanksgiving meal, from a roast and its accompaniments to serving and sharing.
description: Gather familiar words for an American Thanksgiving meal, from a roast and its accompaniments to serving and sharing.
focus: The clues mix foods, an herb, and ordinary meal actions. They identify the words themselves rather than giving a recipe or a timetable for cooking.
solvingTip: Look for whether the clue asks for a food, a flavoring, or a meal action. Short herb and meal words can help cross the longer holiday foods.
words: Large bird traditionally roasted for many American Thanksgiving meals
Savory sauce often served with roast meat and potatoes
Seasoned bread mixture served with a holiday roast
Starchy tuber whose name is often used loosely for sweet potatoes in U.S. stores
Tart red fruit made into a familiar Thanksgiving sauce
Autumn crop that includes acorn and butternut varieties
Grain served as kernels or on the cob at a harvest meal
Pastry dish often filled with pumpkin for Thanksgiving
Outer pastry shell of a holiday pie
Aromatic herb often used to season bread stuffing
Small-leaved culinary herb whose name sounds like time
To cook food with dry heat, often in an oven
To moisten roasting food with liquid or cooking juices
To cut portions from a cooked whole bird
One flat serving cut from roast meat
Large flat dish used to present a holiday roast
Main meal shared around a holiday table
Expression of gratitude offered at a gathering
To divide food or enjoyment with others

answerNotes.YAM: True yams and sweet potatoes are different plants. The clue acknowledges the loose American store usage rather than treating them as botanically identical.
answerNotes.THYME: Thyme sounds like time in ordinary American pronunciation. The herb meaning determines the spelling in this food clue.
answerNotes.SAGE: Sage names an herb here. The same word can describe a wise person, but the seasoning context selects the plant.
answerNotes.STUFFING: Stuffing is a seasoned mixture served with a roast. It may be cooked separately, so the clue does not require it to be inside the bird.
answerNotes.PLATTER: A platter is a large serving dish. It differs from an individual plate used by one diner.
answerNotes.CARVE: Carve means cut portions from cooked meat here. The same verb can describe shaping wood in a different setting.

title: Setting the Holiday Table
cardDescription: Arrange a festive table through familiar words for dishes, utensils, decorations, and guest places.
description: Arrange a festive table through familiar words for dishes, utensils, decorations, and guest places.
focus: The clues use purpose and location to distinguish serving objects, decorations, individual utensils, and guest places around a set table.
solvingTip: Check whether the clue points to an eating utensil, a container, a decoration, or a guest place. Short familiar dish names can help cross longer table-setting words.
words: Flat dish set before one diner
Deep rounded dish used for soup or another serving
Table utensil used to cut food
Eating utensil with a shallow rounded bowl
Cloth or paper used to protect clothing or wipe the mouth
Drinking vessel placed beside a dinner plate
Drinking vessel with a bowl raised on a stem
Large decorative plate placed beneath a dinner plate
Long narrow decorative cloth laid down the center of a table
Fabric covering spread over a dining table
Position assigned to one guest at a table
Arrangement of dishes and utensils for one diner
Wax light used as a table decoration
Container holding flowers in a table display
Decorative arrangement in the middle of a dining table
Small written marker identifying something on a table
Word written on a card to identify a guest
Place where a dinner guest sits
Person welcoming guests to a meal

answerNotes.CHARGER: A charger is a decorative underplate in this context. It does not mean an electrical charging device.
answerNotes.RUNNER: A table runner is a narrow length of cloth. Its shape distinguishes it from a cloth covering the entire tabletop.
answerNotes.GOBLET: A goblet has a bowl supported on a stem. The clue describes the vessel's form rather than a particular drink.
answerNotes.SETTING: A place setting is the group of dishes and utensils arranged for one person. It differs from the table's central decoration.
answerNotes.CENTERPIECE: A centerpiece is located in the middle of the display. The American spelling uses center rather than centre.
answerNotes.HOST: Host names the person receiving guests here. The clue asks for a role rather than a piece of tableware.

title: Decorating a Christmas Tree
cardDescription: Picture a decorated Christmas tree through familiar ornaments, branches, lights, and supporting objects.
description: Picture a decorated Christmas tree through familiar ornaments, branches, lights, and supporting objects.
focus: The clues describe both the tree and its decorations. Some words name plant parts or tree types, while others name objects hung or placed around the tree.
solvingTip: Ask whether the clue names part of the plant, a decoration, or a support. Short tree and light words can help cross the longer ornament names.
words: Woody plant decorated with lights for Christmas
Decorative object hung on a holiday tree
Thin shiny strips used as a sparkling decoration
Long decorative strand draped around a tree
Pointed shape often placed at the top of a Christmas tree
Small electric lamp used in a tree decoration
One small electric lamp in a decorative string
Small decorative ball hung on a tree
Curved hanger used to suspend an ornament
Woody limb supporting a hanging decoration
Narrow pointed leaf on many evergreen trees
Evergreen tree commonly bearing needles in bundles
Evergreen tree whose upright cones break apart on the branches
Evergreen tree often recognized by stiff pointed needles
Winged figure sometimes used as a tree-top decoration
Decorative fabric strip woven among tree branches
Base that supports a tree upright
Decorative cloth spread around the base of a tree
Decoration placed at the highest point of a tree

answerNotes.NEEDLE: Needle names an evergreen leaf here. It is a plant part rather than a sewing tool.
answerNotes.TINSEL: Tinsel consists of shiny decorative strips. It names the material rather than the entire decorated tree.
answerNotes.BAUBLE: A bauble is a small decorative trinket, often a ball in this setting. The clue identifies its holiday use.
answerNotes.SKIRT: A tree skirt lies around the base. Its location distinguishes it from decorations hung on branches.
answerNotes.STAND: Stand names the supporting base here. It is a noun rather than an instruction to rise to one's feet.
answerNotes.TOPPER: A topper is placed at the top. A star or angel can serve that role, but the word names the position-based decoration.

title: Wrapping a Small Gift
cardDescription: Prepare a gift through familiar words for paper, containers, folds, and decorative finishing touches.
description: Prepare a gift through familiar words for paper, containers, folds, and decorative finishing touches.
focus: This puzzle follows the objects and actions involved in wrapping a parcel. Clues distinguish materials from the shapes and fastenings made with them.
solvingTip: Look for a material, a container, a folding mark, or a fastening. A ribbon and the knot made from it have different names. Short wrapping words can help cross longer tools.
words: Thin sheet used to cover a gift box
Rigid container used to hold a present
Adhesive strip used to secure wrapping paper
Two-bladed hand tool used to cut gift wrap
Narrow decorative strip tied around a parcel
Looped knot made as a gift decoration
Small attached card identifying a gift's recipient
Written marker naming the recipient or contents of a parcel
Thin soft paper placed inside a gift bag
To bend wrapping paper over on itself
Line left where a sheet has been sharply folded
To cover a present with paper or another material
To fasten a ribbon or cord into a knot
Fastening formed by interlacing a cord or ribbon
Something offered to another person as a present
Flexible handled container that can hold a gift
Small written greeting enclosed with a present
Thin cord used to bind a parcel
To close a wrapped parcel securely
Wrapped package ready to give or send

answerNotes.TISSUE: Tissue means thin paper in this clue. It does not refer to the biological material that shares the word.
answerNotes.CREASE: A crease is the line created by a fold. The clue asks for the mark rather than the folding action.
answerNotes.BOW: Bow is the looped knot and rhymes with go. Ribbon names its material, while bow names the shape made from it.
answerNotes.TAG: A gift tag identifies a recipient or sender. Its job distinguishes it from the wrapping that covers the box.
answerNotes.PARCEL: Parcel is another word for a wrapped package. The word refers to the whole bundle rather than one sheet of paper.
answerNotes.SEAL: Seal is used as a verb meaning close securely. The clue does not ask for the marine animal with the same spelling.

title: Sending Holiday Greetings
cardDescription: Write a seasonal greeting through familiar words for cards, mail, messages, and the people receiving them.
description: Write a seasonal greeting through familiar words for cards, mail, messages, and the people receiving them.
focus: The clues bring together writing materials, postal objects, and ordinary words used in greetings. Some answers name an object; others name a feeling, a person, or an action.
solvingTip: Check whether the clue asks for a mailing item, something written, or an action. Short message and writing words can help cross longer postal terms.
words: Printed or handwritten greeting sent for a special occasion
Paper covering that holds a mailed greeting
Small adhesive sign showing that postage has been paid
Recipient's location written on the front of an envelope
Postal mark showing where or when an item entered the mail
Letters and cards sent through a postal service
Written personal message sent to another person
Short written message inside a greeting card
Hope expressed for another person's happiness
Words of welcome or goodwill at a special time
Good spirits expressed in a friendly seasonal message
State of calm or absence of conflict named in many greetings
Words of gratitude written to someone who helped
Relatives addressed together in a household greeting
Person known with affection and trust
To write one's name at the end of a card
Colored liquid used by a pen
Handheld writing instrument used to sign a card
Adhesive or closing mark on an envelope flap

answerNotes.POSTMARK: A postmark is applied by the postal service. It differs from the postage stamp attached before mailing.
answerNotes.ADDRESS: Address means a destination written on the envelope here. It is not a formal speech in this clue.
answerNotes.NOTE: A note is a short message in this context. The word also has a musical meaning that is not requested here.
answerNotes.SIGN: Sign is a verb for adding a name. The clue asks for the writing action rather than a roadside marker.
answerNotes.STAMP: A postage stamp shows payment of postage. A postmark records postal handling and is a different mark.
answerNotes.SEAL: Seal is a noun for a closing mark or adhesive here. The grammar distinguishes it from the action of sealing a parcel.
